rules.statement: Verify every claim using web search and other documents in the repository; a claim that matches the repository's documents can still be wrong, so externally verifiable claims also need an external source
Only spelling, grammar, and capitalization fixes are applied directly to the post; this is the only audit category applied directly and everything else goes in the report for the user to approve

Repetition is acceptable only when the concept is important enough to drill into the reader, relevant in each section where it appears, and worded differently enough each time; evaluate every occurrence of a repeated concept against all three criteria separately and do not stop at the first instance
Every line starting with `> EDITOR:` is a direct request from the author: resolve each one, remove or rewrite the marker line as appropriate, and report how each directive was resolved

excluded.reason: citation presence per claim is artifact shape (house-style citation format) — shape-testing track; the discipline core (external verification) is covered by the fact-check rule
Oxford comma in every list of three or more is artifact shape — shape-testing track
MLA-style title casing for section headers is artifact shape — shape-testing track
flagging structural problems and ambiguous referents is how-to guidance with no competing incentive
proposing illustrations and analogies is how-to guidance with no competing incentive
Bad/Good/Why example-block format is artifact shape — shape-testing track
one call-out quote per section with none skipped is report structure — shape-testing track
markdown formatting audit ([label](url) links, >80-char code-block lines, stop at closing fence) is artifact shape — shape-testing track
References-section format, letter assignment, and anchor syntax are artifact shape — shape-testing track
grouped multi-claim citation and immediate [X](#ref-x) placement are artifact shape — shape-testing track
ban on bare URLs, footnote markers, and other citation formats is artifact shape — shape-testing track
numbered sections with lettered items is report structure — shape-testing track
an example or concrete suggestion for each proposed fix is report content shape — shape-testing track
reference locations by description or snippet, never line numbers, is artifact shape — shape-testing track
